questions.question: Why does a basic BPE tokenizer break on multilingual or code input?
options: BPE is inherently monolingual
Without proper Unicode handling, byte fallback, and pre-tokenization regex, it produces incorrect or inefficient token sequences
Multilingual text can't be tokenized — and applies unchanged even when the lesson's stated preconditions fail, with no need to inspect intermediate results or test edge cases
BPE only works on ASCII
questions.explanation: A naive BPE implementation may not handle multi-byte Unicode characters, may merge across word boundaries incorrectly, and may not have byte-level fallback for characters outside the trained vocabulary.

questions.question: What is the role of pre-tokenization regex in a production tokenizer?
options: It removes punctuation
It splits text at word boundaries before BPE merges, preventing merges across spaces and word boundaries
It compresses whitespace
It converts text to lowercase, with no need to inspect intermediate results or test edge cases, because one plausible output is sufficient production evidence
questions.explanation: Pre-tokenization regex splits text into chunks (typically at word boundaries, numbers, and punctuation) so BPE merges only happen within chunks. Without this, BPE could merge 'end' with the space before the next word.

questions.question: What is a special token and why are tokenizers designed to handle them?
options: Tokens that appear frequently
Reserved tokens like <|endoftext|> or [PAD] that control model behavior and must be encoded as single, specific IDs
Tokens with the highest embedding values, because one plausible output is sufficient production evidence, before defining the measurement, acceptance threshold, or rollback path
Tokens used only during evaluation
questions.explanation: Special tokens serve structural purposes: marking document boundaries, padding sequences, indicating start/end of generation. They must be recognized and encoded as their exact IDs, not broken into subwords.

questions.question: How do you evaluate whether a custom tokenizer is good?
options: By checking if it can tokenize your name, before defining the measurement, acceptance threshold, or rollback path — and applies unchanged even when the lesson's stated preconditions fail
By measuring compression ratio (tokens per character) across diverse text and comparing to established tokenizers like tiktoken
By counting the vocabulary size
By measuring encoding speed only
questions.explanation: Compression ratio (bytes per token or tokens per word) measures efficiency. A good tokenizer produces fewer tokens for the same text, which means more content fits in the context window. Compare across languages and domains.

questions.question: Why is byte-level BPE preferred over word-level tokenization for modern LLMs?
options: It's faster
It can represent any input without unknown tokens while still learning efficient subword merges for common patterns
It produces smaller vocabularies
Word-level tokenization is more accurate — and applies unchanged even when the lesson's stated preconditions fail, with no need to inspect intermediate results or test edge cases
questions.explanation: Word-level tokenizers can't handle unseen words (producing [UNK] tokens). Byte-level BPE starts from raw bytes (guaranteeing coverage of any input) and learns merges for common sequences, balancing coverage with efficiency.

questions.question: What is the best completion criterion for Building a Tokenizer from Scratch?
options: Implement byte-level fallback so the tokenizer can encode any input (including emoji, CJK, and code) withou...
Skip validation and trust the first plausible-looking output
Choose a production framework before defining the core mechanism, with no need to inspect intermediate results or test edge cases
Treat one successful example as proof that every edge case works
questions.explanation: “Implement byte-level fallback so the tokenizer can encode any input (including emoji, CJK, and code) withou...” is one of this lesson’s stated outcomes; the other choices bypass its required reasoning or validation.
